verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, to the saints who are in Ephesus and the faithful in Christ Jesus:
verses.1:2: Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ,
verses.1:4: even as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blemish in His sight in love,
verses.1:5: having predestined us for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will,
verses.1:6: to the praise of the glory of His grace, which He graciously bestowed upon us in the Beloved,
verses.1:7: in whom we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of trespasses, according to the riches of His grace,
verses.1:8: which He caused to abound toward us in all wisdom and understanding,
verses.1:9: making known to us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure which He purposed beforehand in Him,
verses.1:10: for the administration of the fullness of the times, to gather up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens and the things upon the earth—in Him,
verses.1:11: in whom we also were chosen as a heritage, having been predestined according to the purpose of Him who works all things according to the counsel of His will,
verses.1:12: that we who first set our hope in Christ should be to the praise of His glory;
verses.1:13: in whom you also, having heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation—in whom also, having believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
verses.1:14: who is the pledge of our inheritance, for the redemption of the acquired possession, to the praise of His glory.
verses.1:15: For this reason I also, having heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus and that which is toward all the saints,
verses.1:16: do not cease giving thanks on your behalf, remembering you in my prayers,
verses.1:17: that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may grant to you a spirit of wisdom and of revelation in the full knowledge of Him,
verses.1:18: with the eyes of your heart enlightened, that you may know what is the hope of His calling, what are the riches of the glory of His inheritance in the saints,
verses.1:19: and what is the surpassing greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of the might of His strength,
verses.1:20: which He has worked in Christ, raising Him from the dead and seating Him at His right hand in the heavenly places,
verses.1:21: far above every principality and authority and power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in that which is to come;
verses.1:22: and He subjected all things beneath His feet, and gave Him as head over all things to the church,
verses.1:23: which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all things in all.
verses.2:1: And you, being dead in your trespasses and sins,
verses.2:2: in which you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit now working in the sons of disobedience;
verses.2:3: among whom we all also once lived in the lusts of our flesh, carrying out the desires of the flesh and of the thoughts, and were by nature children of wrath, even as the rest;
verses.2:4: but God, being rich in mercy, on account of His great love with which He loved us,
verses.2:5: even while we were dead in trespasses, made us alive together with Christ—by grace you have been saved—
verses.2:6: and raised us up together, and seated us together in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
verses.2:7: that in the ages to come He might display the surpassing riches of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.
verses.2:8: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not from yourselves—it is the gift of God;
verses.2:9: not from works, lest anyone boast.
verses.2:10: For we are His handiwork, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God made ready beforehand that we should walk in them.
verses.2:11: Therefore remember that once you, the Gentiles in the flesh, who are called "Uncircumcision" by what is called "Circumcision" made by hands in the flesh—
verses.2:12: that you were at that time separate from Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers to the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world.
verses.2:13: But now in Christ Jesus, you who formerly were far off have been brought near in the blood of Christ.
verses.2:14: For He Himself is our peace, who made both one and broke down the dividing wall of the barrier—the enmity—in His flesh,
verses.2:15: having abolished the law of commandments in ordinances, that He might create the two in Himself into one new man, making peace,
verses.2:16: and might reconcile them both in one body to God through the cross, having slain the enmity in it;
verses.2:17: and having come, He preached peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near;
verses.2:18: because through Him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father.
verses.2:19: So then you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God,
verses.2:20: having been built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus Himself as the chief cornerstone,
verses.2:21: in whom the entire building, being closely fitted together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord,
verses.2:22: in whom you also are being built together into a habitation of God in the Spirit.
verses.3:1: For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles—
verses.3:2: if indeed you have heard of the stewardship of the grace of God given to me for you;
verses.3:3: by revelation the mystery was made known to me, just as I have written beforehand in brief,
verses.3:4: by which, as you read, you are able to perceive my insight into the mystery of Christ,
verses.3:5: which in other generations was not made known to the sons of men, as it has now been revealed to His holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit:
verses.3:6: that the Gentiles are fellow heirs, and members of the same body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel,
verses.3:7: of which I was made a minister according to the gift of the grace of God that was given to me according to the working of His power—
verses.3:8: to me, less than the least of all saints, this grace was given—to proclaim to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
verses.3:9: and to enlighten all as to what is the stewardship of the mystery that was hidden from the ages in God, who created all things,
verses.3:10: so that now the manifold wisdom of God might be made known through the church to the principalities and authorities in the heavenly places,
verses.3:11: according to the purpose of the ages which He accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord,
verses.3:12: in whom we have boldness and access in confidence through faith in Him.
verses.3:13: Therefore I ask that you not lose heart in my tribulations on your behalf, which is your glory.
verses.3:14: For this cause I bow my knees to the Father,
verses.3:15: from whom every family in the heavens and upon the earth is named,
verses.3:16: that He may grant to you, according to the riches of His glory, to be made strong with power through His Spirit in the inner man,
verses.3:17: so that Christ may dwell through faith in your hearts in love; being rooted and founded,
verses.3:18: that you may have full strength to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and height and depth,
verses.3:19: and to know the love of Christ which transcends knowledge, so that you may be filled to all the fullness of God.
verses.3:20: Now to Him who is able to do beyond all things, immeasurably more than what we ask or conceive, according to the power that is working within us,
verses.3:21: to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.
verses.4:1: Therefore I, the prisoner in the Lord, exhort you to walk worthy of the calling by which you were called,
verses.4:2: with all lowliness of mind and meekness, with longsuffering, bearing with one another in love,
verses.4:3: diligently striving to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
verses.4:4: There is one body and one Spirit, even as you also were called in one hope of your calling;
verses.4:5: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;
verses.4:6: one God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in all.
verses.4:7: Now to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
verses.4:8: Therefore it says, "Having ascended on high, He led captivity captive; He gave gifts to men."
verses.4:9: Now this, "He ascended"—what does it mean, except that He also descended into the lower parts of the earth?
verses.4:10: He who descended is Himself also the One who ascended far above all the heavens, so that He might fill all things.
verses.4:11: And He Himself gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, and some as shepherds and teachers,
verses.4:12: for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry, toward the building up of the body of Christ,
verses.4:13: until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the full knowledge of the Son of God, to a mature man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ;
verses.4:14: so that we may no longer be infants, tossed by waves and carried about by every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, in craftiness toward deceitful scheming;
verses.4:15: rather, speaking the truth in love, we may grow up in every way into Him who is the head, Christ,
verses.4:16: from whom the whole body, being framed together and knit together through every joint of supply, according to the working in due measure of each single part, brings about the growth of the body for the building up of itself in love.
verses.4:17: Therefore this I say and solemnly testify in the Lord, that you must no longer walk just as the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their mind,
verses.4:18: being darkened in their understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them, because of the hardness of their heart;
verses.4:19: who, having become callous, gave themselves over to licentiousness for the practice of all uncleanness with greediness.
verses.4:20: But you did not learn Christ in this way,
verses.4:21: if indeed you heard Him and were taught in Him, just as truth is in Jesus:
verses.4:22: that you lay aside, with respect to your former manner of life, the old man who is being corrupted according to the lusts of deceit,
verses.4:23: and that you be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
verses.4:24: and that you put on the new man, created according to God in righteousness and holiness of the truth.
verses.4:25: Therefore, having laid aside falsehood, speak truth, each one with his neighbor, for we are members of one another.
verses.4:26: Be angry, and do not sin; do not let the sun set upon your wrath,
verses.4:27: and do not give place to the devil.
verses.4:28: Let the one who steals steal no more, but rather let him labor, working with his hands what is good, so that he may have something to share with the one who has need.
verses.4:29: Let no corrupt speech come forth from your mouth, but only what is good for edification according to the need, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
verses.4:30: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
verses.4:31: Let all bitterness and fury and wrath and outcry and slander be taken away from you, together with all malice.
verses.4:32: And become kind toward one another, tenderhearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
verses.5:1: Therefore, become imitators of God, as beloved children,
verses.5:2: and walk in love, just as Christ also loved you and gave Himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a fragrant aroma.
verses.5:3: But sexual immorality and all impurity or covetousness must not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints,
verses.5:4: nor obscenity, nor foolish talk, nor coarse jesting, which are not proper, but rather thanksgiving.
verses.5:5: For this you know with certainty, that no sexually immoral person, nor unclean person, nor covetous man—that is, an idolater—has any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.
verses.5:6: Let no one deceive you with empty words; for on account of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience.
verses.5:7: Therefore do not become partakers with them;
verses.5:8: for you were formerly darkness, yet now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light
verses.5:9: (for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness and righteousness and truth),
verses.5:10: proving what is well-pleasing to the Lord;
verses.5:11: and do not share in the unfruitful works of darkness, but instead even expose them;
verses.5:12: for it is shameful even to speak of the things done by them in secret.
verses.5:13: Yet all things, when exposed by the light, are made manifest; for everything that is made manifest is light.
verses.5:14: Therefore it says, "Awake, O sleeper, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall shine upon you."
verses.5:15: Watch carefully therefore how you walk, not as unwise, but as wise,
verses.5:16: redeeming the time, for the days are evil.
verses.5:17: For this reason, do not become foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.
verses.5:18: And do not become drunk with wine, in which is debauchery, but be filled with the Spirit,
verses.5:19: speaking among yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody with your heart to the Lord,
verses.5:20: giving thanks at all times for all things, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to God and the Father,
verses.5:21: being subject to one another in the fear of Christ.
verses.5:22: Wives, be in subjection to your own husbands, as to the Lord;
verses.5:23: for the husband is head of the wife, even as Christ also is head of the church, He Himself being the Savior of the body.
verses.5:24: Yet as the church is subject to Christ, so also let wives be to their husbands in everything.
verses.5:25: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself up for her,
verses.5:26: so that He might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word,
verses.5:27: so that He Himself might present to Himself the church in splendor, having neither spot nor wrinkle nor any such thing, but that she might be holy and without blemish.
verses.5:28: In this same way husbands also ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his own wife loves himself;
verses.5:29: for no one ever hated his own flesh, but instead nourishes and cherishes it, even as Christ also does the church,
verses.5:30: for we are members of His body.
verses.5:31: For this cause a man shall leave father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.
verses.5:32: This mystery is great, yet I am speaking with reference to Christ and the church.
verses.5:33: Nevertheless, let each one of you individually love his own wife just as himself, and let the wife see that she reverences her husband.
verses.6:1: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is just.
verses.6:2: "Honor your father and your mother"—which is the first commandment with a promise—
verses.6:3: "that it may go well with you, and you shall be long-lived upon the earth."
verses.6:4: And fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but nurture them in the discipline and admonition of the Lord.
verses.6:5: Bondservants, obey your masters according to the flesh with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as to Christ,
verses.6:6: not by way of eye-service as pleasers of men, but as bondservants of Christ doing the will of God, from the soul
verses.6:7: serving with goodwill, as to the Lord and not to men,
verses.6:8: knowing that whatever good thing each one does, he shall receive this back from the Lord, whether bondservant or free.
verses.6:9: And masters, do the same things toward them, laying aside threatening, knowing that the Master of both them and you is in the heavens, and there is no partiality with Him.
verses.6:10: Finally, be strengthened in the Lord and in the might of His strength.
verses.6:11: Put on the complete armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the stratagems of the devil;
verses.6:12: for our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the principalities, against the authorities, against the world-rulers of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.
verses.6:13: Therefore take up the complete armor of God, that you may be able to resist in the evil day, and having accomplished all things, to stand.
verses.6:14: Stand therefore, having girded your loins with truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
verses.6:15: and having shod your feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace,
verses.6:16: in all circumstances taking up the shield of faith, with which you shall be able to extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one;
verses.6:17: and receive the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God,
verses.6:18: through all prayer and supplication, praying at every season in the Spirit, and to this end keeping watch with all perseverance and supplication for all the saints,
verses.6:19: and on my behalf, that a word may be given to me in the opening of my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel,
verses.6:20: for which I serve as an ambassador in a chain, that in it I may speak with boldness, as I must speak.
verses.6:21: Now that you also may know the things concerning me and how I am faring, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will make all things known to you,
verses.6:22: whom I have sent to you for this very purpose, that you may know the things concerning us, and that he may encourage your hearts.
verses.6:23: Peace be to the brethren, and love together with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.6:24: Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption.

notes.1:4: In Greek, "in love" can either conclude verse 4 ("holy and without blemish in His sight in love") or introduce the participle in verse 5 ("in love having predestined us").
notes.1:10: The Greek verb rendered "to gather up" (anakephalaiosasthai) literally means "to sum up" or "to bring together under one head."
notes.1:11: The Greek passive verb eklerothemen can mean either "we were chosen as a heritage" (as God's own portion) or "we obtained an inheritance."
notes.1:15: The Greek text omits the word "love" found in later manuscripts, leaving the article to refer back to the Ephesians' faith (or faithfulness) toward all the saints.
notes.2:8: The neuter demonstrative "this" (touto) does not match the feminine gender of "grace" or "faith," indicating that the whole salvation by grace through faith is the gift of God.
notes.2:14: In the Greek text, "the enmity" stands in apposition to the dividing wall broken down in Christ's flesh, though some construe it as the object of "having abolished" in verse 15.
notes.2:16: The Greek phrase en auto at the end of the verse can mean either "in it" (referring to the cross) or "in Himself."
notes.3:9: The Greek text reads "stewardship" (oikonomia) rather than "fellowship" (koinonia) and omits "through Jesus Christ" at the end of the verse.
notes.3:12: The Greek phrase dia tes pisteos autou is traditionally rendered "through faith in Him," though it may also be understood as "through His faithfulness."
notes.3:14: The Greek text reads simply "to the Father," omitting "of our Lord Jesus Christ" found in later manuscripts. Verses 14 and 15 feature a Greek wordplay between "Father" (pater) and "family" (patria).
notes.3:17: Following the punctuation of the Greek text, "in love" is joined to Christ dwelling in believers' hearts, though it is often construed with "rooted and founded."
notes.4:8: Paul cites Psalm 68:18 (LXX 67:19), reading "He gave gifts to men" rather than "you received gifts among men" as in the Hebrew and Septuagint texts. The critical Greek text also omits "and" before "He gave."
notes.4:9: The Greek phrase "the lower parts of the earth" is variously understood as referring to the earth itself in contrast to heaven, to the realm of the dead, or to the depths of the incarnation.
notes.4:11: The Greek term rendered "shepherds" (poimenas) is traditionally translated "pastors" in ecclesiastical usage; the shared syntax of "shepherds and teachers" suggests closely related or overlapping ministries.
notes.4:29: The phrase "for edification according to the need" translates a compressed Greek genitive (pros oikodomen tes chreias, literally "for building up of the need"), indicating speech fitted to build up hearers as the occasion requires.
notes.5:2: The critical Greek text shifts from "loved you" (humas) to "gave Himself up for us" (hemon), preserving the pronoun variation of the earliest manuscripts rather than harmonizing them.
notes.5:9: The earliest Greek manuscripts read "the fruit of the light" rather than "the fruit of the Spirit," directly continuing the light-and-darkness contrast of verse 8.
notes.5:13: The Greek participle phaneroumenon is debated as either passive ("everything that is made manifest is light") or middle ("everything that makes manifest is light"), and "by the light" may modify either "exposed" or "made manifest."
notes.5:22: The earliest Greek manuscripts have no explicit verb in this verse, carrying over "being subject" from verse 21; the verb "be in subjection" is supplied for English sense.
notes.5:30: The earliest Greek manuscripts end at "members of His body"; later manuscripts expand the verse with "of His flesh and of His bones," echoing Genesis 2:23.
notes.6:9: The Greek word kyrios means both "master" and "Lord," creating a deliberate wordplay between earthly masters and the heavenly Master. The critical text reads "of both them and you," underscoring Christ's impartial authority over bondservant and master alike.
notes.6:12: The Greek text places "blood and flesh" in that order and reads "of this darkness" without the phrase "of this age" found in later manuscripts.
notes.6:16: The critical text reads en pasin ("in all circumstances" or "with all of these") rather than epi pasin ("above all").
notes.6:24: Literally "in incorruption" or "in imperishability," indicating an undying, incorruptible love for Christ. The earliest manuscripts conclude the epistle here without "Amen."
